ui.note: Document neutral sign-up followed by explicit sign-in, including email-bound invitation and pending native approval journeys in all six locales. Document local timer persistence, exclusive server-timed spans, explicit offline proof and deferred completion reconciliation after reload. Start and resume now anchor elapsed time at the action. Completion replay, dismissible logging errors, server permissions, timestamp validation and persisted formats remain unchanged. Import completion and conflict transfer focus during the DOM commit; moving focus during a status retry cancels the handoff, which also rechecks focus before committing. Import inputs, acknowledgment and persistence are unchanged. Document the browser connection requirement on opening or reloading, automatic and manual retries for transport failures, and continued offline editing in already-open tabs. HTTP session and startup refusals keep their existing behavior; no cached identity or offline startup is added. Once the session has resolved, a signed-out refetch after a sign-up or sign-in attempt no longer remounts Login, while the first fetch keeps the boot skeleton, so the entered email, the sign-up notice and sign-in errors stay visible; no documented flow changes.

release.note: Prepare the first beta, 0.1.0-beta.1 with Android code 13, retain the existing signing certificate and documentation epoch, align release commands, and describe the remaining prerelease and native qualification limits. Generated publication notes now describe a prerelease rather than an alpha.

configuration.note: Keep the beta.1 app and Zero image pair. Document the private focus clock schema, migration ownership and runtime USAGE plus SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE grants. Exclude this schema from Zero publications; retain the existing shard grants for runtime and migrator.

deployment.note: Preserve beta.1 packaging, app/Zero pairing and cluster qualification limits. Compose and CNPG initialize a migration-owned private schema with restricted runtime DML; the role runbook covers custom roles, upgrades and rebuilding retained Zero caches that copied the former public clock table.

native.note: Document desktop cold offline activation from complete unexpired evidence in the OS credential store, exact session binding, fail-closed verification and revocation markers, and native token refresh on socket retry. Existing records need one complete online start; downgrades require signing out stored accounts before installing an older build. Retain queued edits, refuse fallback for trust, HTTP, validation or storage failures, and keep platform runtime qualification explicit. Android cached activation policy is unchanged. Every authenticated native request now persists a refusal fence before I/O, including attachment, notification, cleanup and sync-handshake requests. Binary keyring chunks stay within the Windows blob limit, share credential references, and use a bounded recovery journal. Both earlier protected-record formats require fresh online evidence after upgrade; downgrades require OS credential-manager cleanup. The desktop TLS refusal test fixture now carries a fixed non-secret password because macOS refuses empty-password PKCS#12 imports; test-only, no runtime or documented behavior change.

authentication.note: OAuth registration denials preserve their stable policy code through Better Auth callback redirects. Native browser sign-in retains the grant ID and displays the localized policy message. Document periodic stream revalidation after session revocation; HTTP authorization remains checked against live session state. Invitations remain HTTPS browser links with fragment tokens and backward-compatible acceptance; native task scheme handling is unchanged. Document the current account name, identity update validation, synced display behavior, and managed-account normalization with JSON validation errors. Production startup validates secret length and retained JWKS decryption. The authentication guide links the stopped-replica secret rotation procedure instead of direct replacement. Browser sign-in checks the per-IP ceiling before creating IP-plus-email buckets. The handoff and trusted-proxy guides document that order, unchanged limits and batch-drained cleanup; docs/security.md records the body bound and unchanged TOTP lockout. The authentication guides already changed in this branch document neutral public email sign-up, explicit sign-in without SMTP, admission policy and unchanged native approval. This follow-up preserves that public and native protocol: only identity and password fields reach account creation, and persistence failures use the existing neutral result and timing floor. docs/security.md now describes discarded fields and operator-visible failure logs. No new setup, recovery, native trust, account admission, or credential storage procedure is introduced; managed-account creation retains explicit failures. Unexpected registration-policy failures are logged and return a generic unavailable error instead of a policy refusal carrying the raw message; documented refusals are unchanged.

compatibility.note: Move the RLS-protected clock table to server_private, outside default and explicit public Zero publications, while preserving timing evidence and updating the bounded expiry function. Exclusive spans and full server-observed duration remain required. Auto-cycle starts only after prior completion replay settles; per-interval reconciliation expiry never permits an unqualified observer to discard another tab's proof opportunity.
compatibility.upgrade: Apply all focus migrations with Zero stopped, verify private runtime grants, reload clients and start fresh intervals. Earlier overlapping start evidence is invalidated. Rebuild retained disposable Zero caches that copied the former public clock table, then verify fresh-client sync. Existing focus sessions need no conversion.
compatibility.backup: Keep coordinated full-database and attachment backups before migration. Restore acknowledgement and private clock tables together with schema grants. Missing or expired evidence rejects server-proof completions; persisted browser flags do not authorize fallback. Attachment ciphertext and key envelopes are unchanged.
compatibility.rollback: The preceding published application ignores the added tables and can retain the migrated database. Intermediate focus builds querying public clocks or timestamps in acknowledgements need a matching schema rollback from coordinated backup; do not restore an old database over newer focus sessions merely to downgrade.
compatibility.clientVersions: Reload updated web and native clients after upgrade. Legacy clients without interval IDs keep legacy logging; interval-ID clients need the proof marker for offline completions. Unmarked pending completions require server evidence. Auto-cycle waits for replay settlement, and observers never discard an interval without proof. Offline and legacy personal totals remain client-reported.

clients.note: Document the retained runtime notice manifest, exact source URLs and SHA-256 checksums, extracted-archive integrity qualification, and unchanged incomplete runtime license coverage and binary publication block.
